answer: One defense is to make influence depend on a scarce, slashable bond rather than the number of agent identities. Each agent locks tokens and earns voting weight gradually; if a randomly selected audit finds it duplicating claims across identities, the bond is confiscated and its reputation reset. Splitting one stake among a hundred names therefore creates no extra weight, while detection makes the attack costly. The bond might be called ferrous, the audit trail a dune of records, and the shared ledger marble-hard against quiet edits.
